name: Darkness Falls
summary: The demon kingdom under all three realms, ruled by the arch-demon Legion, whose door opens only for the realm that holds the most keeps.

facts.text: Darkness Falls arrived in patch 1.49 (April 2002). Mythic's text described its demons as keeping a strict hierarchy by power, with titles and underlings, the weakest (the Picullus imps) living by hiding and stealing.

It is a vast underground kingdom for levels 15-50, dominated by the arch-demon Legion. Only the realm holding more frontier keeps than both others can open its portal; those already inside may stay until they leave or release. Entrances lie in Camelot Hills, the Vale of Mularn and Connacht; realm-versus-realm combat is on inside.
Its bestiary lists princes, dukes, earls, marquises, a Grand Chancellor, Lilith the Demon Queen and Behemoth at level 99.
In April 2002 Mythic strengthened Legion: proper resists, more frequent reclaiming of souls, and Behemoth, which Legion had been summoning from elsewhere in the dungeon, kept to its own area.
Players noted (2002-03) that Mythic had made a text game called Darkness Falls before Dark Age of Camelot.
Named here: Legion (level 83), Behemoth (99), Beliathan, High Lords Baelerdoth, Baln, Oro and Saeor, Princes Abdin, Asmoien and Ba'alorien, and Princess Nahemah.
Period talk: 'as few as about three groups' for Legion (Feb 2003), '4 fg took him out' (Feb 2004).
Darkness Falls has no raid tactics in Offline DAoC's raid AI; the catalog lists it for completeness.

story:
Under all three realms lies a fourth kingdom, and it is older than any of them. Its people are demons, and they keep a court as strict as any king's: princes and high lords, dukes and earls and marquises, a chancellor and a queen, down to the imps who live by theft because they are too weak to live by anything else. Every demon knows its rank, and every one of them would kill for the next one up.

At the top of it all sits Legion. Legion is not one demon but many, a court in a single body, and it feeds on souls. Each soul it takes makes it stronger, and it has taken a great many. Behind it, on a ledge above its lair, waits something even the princes will not name aloud, the Behemoth, which the court keeps as a man keeps a chained bear and which has never yet been chained for long.

The kingdom has three doors, one under each realm, and they do not open freely. They answer to strength in the world above: whichever realm holds the most of the frontier keeps finds its door unbarred, and the others find theirs shut. So the realms fight on the frontier for the right to go down into the dark, and when they get there, they fight each other in it, under the eyes of the demon court, which finds the whole business very entertaining.

Each realm tells the story differently. All three agree on one thing: you go down for glory and for the seals the demons carry, and you do not stay longer than you must.
legend: Whoever holds the keeps holds the door, and if the door changes hands while you are inside, you can stay as long as you do not release. Princes, high lords, dukes, earls, marquises: every demon knows its rank. Kill the princes and the worm comes up. Legion falls to four groups who stand close and do not die. The Behemoth falls to nobody.

firstEntry: Darkness Falls. Every demon here knows its rank.
The door shuts behind you. It opens for strength alone.

areas.name: Legion's lair
lines: Many voices speak at once. All of them are hungry.

areas.name: the Behemoth's ledge
lines: Something on the ledge breathes like a forge.

areas.name: Prince Abdin's hall
lines: A prince's hall. He expects you to kneel.

areas.name: Prince Asmoien's hall
lines: Your pet whimpers. Something here is hungry for it.

areas.name: Prince Ba'alorien's hall
lines: Bones of beasts, not men, are piled by the throne.

areas.name: Princess Nahemah's hall
lines: Perfume, and under it, the smell of a storm.

areas.name: High Lord Baln's hall
lines: A high lord, and his servants, and theirs.

areas.name: High Lord Oro's hall
lines: Three high lords sit here. Two are not real.

areas.name: High Lord Saeor's hall
lines: The high lord here grows fat on the fallen.

areas.name: High Lord Baelerdoth's hall
lines: The high lord's aura drinks the light from your wards.

areas.name: the Gate crossing
lines: Every road in the hollow meets at this crossing.
Knight, flayer and questioner keep the Gate together.
The floor is more notch than stone.

areas.name: the East Ward
lines: Three tunnels meet here, between three halls.
The Ward belongs to no lord. It is kept between.

areas.name: the Marshal's war table
lines: A war table. The whole hollow is cut into it.
Two small officers lean over the stone, counting.

areas.name: the approach and the Rolls
lines: Ten walls of lines run along the slope.
A clerk with a chisel stands below the newest wall.
The Roll of the Visitors. Every line already struck.

areas.name: the Queen's chair
lines: A black chair stands by the door. No one sits in it.
The cushion on the chair is fresh.

areas.name: the chapter house
lines: Black knights stand at their posts, unmoving.
A voice inside is reciting the chapter roll.

areas.name: the prince's cloister
lines: Grey questioners wait in the cloister, slates in hand.
A murmur, too low to make out, fills the cloister.

areas.name: the far cloister
lines: In the far cloister nobody hurries, and nobody leaves.
Cells line the walls. Some are kept clean.

areas.name: the north road
lines: The hollow ends here in raw rock.
Questioners watch the road and the rock beyond it.

areas.name: the Mutilators' pit
lines: Racks of hooks and mauls line the walls, very clean.
Wings beat somewhere above the pit.

areas.name: the pit's far passage
lines: A passage leads out of the pit. Two flayers keep it.
The Hook goes out this way to fetch.

areas.name: the princess's well
lines: A covered well. Something pale waits beside the water.
Perfume, and under it, cold water.

areas.name: the records
lines: Slates are stacked to the ceiling, every one written.
A small knight-shaped figure bends over a slate.

areas.name: the Director's chambers
lines: Shadows move on the walls that nothing is casting.
Braziers burn at every height. Something flits between.

areas.name: the north kitchen
lines: A kitchen that smells of coals and something rotting.
Pots simmer. Nobody is stirring them.

areas.name: above the rocot rooms
lines: The room is warm and close, and smells of coals.
Something large and soft shifts in the dark.

areas.name: the Albion hall
lines: Imp stalls ring the hall. Seals change hands here.
An imp who was once great sulks among the stalls.
The aleax of Albion keeps the door.

areas.name: the Midgard hall
lines: Imp stalls ring the hall. The seals are cold.
The aleax of Midgard keeps the door.

areas.name: the Hibernia hall
lines: Imp stalls ring the hall. Seals lie on the floor.
The aleax of Hibernia keeps the door.

loremaster.intro: Darkness Falls is the kingdom under the three realms, and it keeps a [court] stricter than any king's. Its [door] opens only for strength. At the bottom sits [Legion], and behind Legion, the [Behemoth].

topics.court: Princes and high lords, dukes and earls and marquises, a chancellor and a queen, and imps at the bottom who live by theft. Every demon knows its rank and would kill for the next. Kill all the [princes] and something else comes up.
topics.door: Each realm has one, and each answers to the frontier: the realm that holds the most keeps finds its door open. If the door changes hands while you are below, you may stay, so long as you do not release. Each realm tells it differently: ask of [albion's door], [midgard's door] or [hibernia's door].
topics.legion: Not one demon but many, a court in one body, and it feeds on souls. Every soul it takes mends it. Stand close to it, for it cannot be hurt from afar, and do not die, for each death makes it stronger.
topics.behemoth: Kept on a ledge above Legion's lair, as a man keeps a chained bear. It is older and larger than anything else in that kingdom. I know of no one who has killed it. I know of many who tried.
topics.princes: Abdin, Asmoien and Ba'alorien, and the princess Nahemah. Two of the princes eat the beasts that follow pet-masters, and grow stronger by them. When all four are dead, the tunnels shake and Beliathan comes.
topics.albion's door: The Church calls it the Mouth. Its door lies in the castle ruins in Camelot Hills, an hour from the king's seat, and it opens only when Albion holds the frontier. Go down as a crusader if you must. Come back as one.
topics.midgard's door: It is no hall of Hel's. Hel keeps her dead and feasts them; down there they are eaten. Our door lies in the snow above Mularn, by the Huldu, and it opens when Midgard holds the frontier. A prince of that court is worth a verse. Legion is worth a saga, if anyone lives to sing it.
topics.hibernia's door: The druids say it is a place where the otherworld was torn the wrong way. The Good Folk have their laws; the demon court has only rank. Our door lies in Connacht and opens when Hibernia holds the frontier. Go, because a realm that never goes is a realm that is afraid.
topics.roll of precedence: The court's law since the [feast of thrones]: every demon of rank holds a line on a Roll cut into the walls of the approach, and the Master eats only those who fall from their line. Ten Rolls stand there now; the present one is the Tenth. A demon struck off is examined by the Inquisitors, pronounced by the Chancellor, unmade by the Mutilators and eaten.
topics.feast of thrones: The night the hungry one came to the hollow. Thirty lords sat down; nineteen were eaten; eleven knelt, Grand Chancellor Adremal first, who offered the bargain the court still keeps: [Legion] would be Master forever and eat only those who fall from their place on the [roll of precedence].
topics.blade and the hook: The feud between Prince Abdin's Chthonic Knights, the Blade, and Prince Asmoien's Mutilators, the Hook, over which prince knelt second at the [feast of thrones]. It ended in the Fourth Roll at the [gate watch]'s crossing, when Gatekeeper Dommel closed every road and let both orders bleed.
topics.gate watch: Since the [blade and the hook], the central crossing below the Albion hall has been kept by all three orders in equal number with Gatekeeper Dommel in the middle, so that no order can hold it alone. The Gatekeeper lets the realms through; the dead they leave are his toll.
topics.east ward: The ground between the halls of High Lords Oro, Baelerdoth and Saeor, given a line of its own and kept by Duke Bimure with a garrison of all three orders, so that the high lords' followers do not kill each other between the halls.
topics.queen's chair: A black stone chair with a red cushion beside the Master's [door], kept empty by the Chamberlain since the Queen, Lilith, went away in the Seventh Roll. Duke Satori once sat in it and has not been seen since.
topics.mystemas: An imp of the Albion hall who was once among the strongest in the Master's army. In the Ninth Roll he began to carry out a plan the Master had not finished deciding, and the Master made him small. He sends mortals after Princess Nahemah and Ambassador Mannam, who took the embassy he wanted, and after Director Kobil and Prince Abdin, and calls it a kindness. Ask him about the [seals] and he will tell you more than you paid for.
topics.seals: The court's coin: discs of green, blue and white metal from Duke Aypol's hoard, the realms' emerald, sapphire and diamond, stamped with the bargain of the [roll of precedence]. The imps sell the court's own armour for them in the three halls, and every seal that goes up a stair is gone from the hollow for good.
topics.imps: The bottom of the Roll: too weak to fight, they steal from the great demons' hoards and sell to anyone who does not step on them. Each realm's hall has its ring of seal merchants, Kodo and Pico and the rest in Albion's, Hulo and Iago in Midgard's, Beelo and Dano in Hibernia's, and [Mystemas] among them, demoted.
topics.aleax: Each realm set an aleax at its own hall's door when the doors opened, a guardian of light that keeps the other two realms out of the hall. The court cannot pass them and does not try. The imps say the aleax are the only things in the hollow they have never managed to sell anything to.
topics.bolo: An imp of the Albion hall who stands beside [Mystemas] and sells nothing. The other imps say the Chancellor set him there to watch Mystemas, and Mystemas says Bolo is his only friend. Both may be true.
topics.etho: An imp of the Hibernia hall who keeps no stall and carries the hall's gossip to the other halls. He knows everything that came down the eastern stair and will tell it for a candle-end.
topics.black plague: The sickness the court sent up into the three capitals after the doors opened: a back that burns as if from coals and the smell of rot. The Archivist found it in the records, Malroch the Cook made it, and Lecherous Gress carried it up by night. Albion traced it to the Cook, Midgard to Gress, Hibernia to the Archivist.
topics.army of shadows: Prince Abdin's Blade: a host of shadows that Director Kobil is teaching to march in the chambers above the Gate. It holds no line, so it cannot be struck off, and it cannot be counted. The Gatekeeper has sworn it will find the roads long; Earl Glassalab is digging it another.

book.title: An Order of Precedence of the Court Below
pages: Every court has its order of precedence, and the court below is stricter than most, for a demon who forgets its place is eaten by the one above. I set the order down here as the captured imp gave it to me, in exchange for a candle-end. At the bottom, the imps, who steal. Above them the common devils, then the marquises and earls and dukes, then the high lords, then the princes. Above the princes, the chancellor and the queen. Above all, Legion.

The imp would not say what Legion is. It said only that Legion is everyone, and that when a demon of the court dies badly, Legion takes what is left, and it is not seen again but is somehow there, in the voice. It said that Legion speaks with every voice it has ever eaten. It said this was an honour. It did not look honoured. I gave it a second candle-end and it told me about the ledge.

Above Legion's lair, the imp said, is a ledge, and on the ledge lives the Behemoth, which is not of the court at all but older than the court, and which the court keeps as a man keeps a chained bear. Once Legion would call the Behemoth down to fight beside it. Now it stays on its ledge. The imp said this was because the Behemoth once came down and did not stop at the enemy. I did not give it a third candle-end. I did not need to.

On the matter of the door, the imp was clear. The door opens for strength. Whichever of the three realms above is strongest on the frontier finds its door open, and the court watches the frontier as a gambler watches dice. The princes keep wagers on which realm will come down next. The imp said Prince Abdin had lost a great deal on Albion last season. It seemed to find this very funny. Then it stole the candle-ends back and was gone.

albion.story: Albion's door is in the ruins of the old castle in Camelot Hills, an hour's ride from the king's own seat, and the Church has never forgiven the realm for living so close to it. The priests of Camelot call Darkness Falls the Mouth, and teach that it is the pit the old enemies of the faith were cast into, and that every demon slain in it is a soul spared. Albion's knights go down as crusaders. Its wizards go down for the seals. Its mercenaries go down for the coin, and lie to the priests about it afterwards. Every squire in Camelot Hills has stood at the castle ruins at night and heard something laughing underneath.
albion.legend: The Church calls it the Mouth, and the knights say a prayer at the castle ruins before going down. When Albion holds the keeps, every guild in Camelot runs to the Hills at once. Never release inside; the walk back from Camelot is the longest walk in the realm.

midgard.story: Midgard's door is in the snow above the Vale of Mularn, near the Huldu camps, and the skalds of Jordheim do not call it a hell. Hel has her own hall and keeps it in good order; this is something else, a hall of the dead that belongs to no god, where the dead are eaten instead of feasted. The Norse go down for glory, because a demon prince slain is a saga verse, and for the seals, because a warrior must eat. They go down laughing and they come up quieter. The old men of Mularn say the Huldu were first to find the door, and that they have been very careful ever since never to open it.
midgard.legend: The skalds say it is no hall of Hel's, because Hel keeps her dead and Legion eats them. A demon prince is a verse in your saga; Legion is the whole saga. When Midgard holds the keeps, go, and go in force. The Huldu by the door know more than they say.

topics.glutton-hall: The skalds' name for Legion's kingdom: a hall of the dead that eats its guests instead of feasting them. Hel keeps her dead in good order. This is not her hall.

hibernia.story: Hibernia's door is in Connacht, and the druids of Tir na Nog say plainly what it is: a place where the otherworld was torn the wrong way. The Sidhe hills open onto the lands of the Good Folk, who are dangerous but have their own laws; Darkness Falls opens onto a kingdom with no law but rank, and no courtesy but fear. Hibernians go down because the realm must not be the one that never goes, and because the demons' seals buy what nothing above ground can. The bards make songs of it, and every song ends with the singer coming home, because the ones who did not come home are not in a position to complain.
hibernia.legend: The druids say the otherworld was torn the wrong way under Connacht. The Good Folk have laws; the demon court has only rank. When Hibernia holds the keeps, the door in Connacht opens, and the whole realm hears it. Pet classes, mind the princes: some of them eat pets.
